text:
maria: heads up — found a subtle correctness window when the prefetch subsystem delegates to a remote lease owner. description: prefetch hands off responsibility via a DelegationToken while the lease epoch can still advance.

aj: can you sketch the problematic interleaving?

maria: sure. timeline: A holds lease epoch 42, prefetch creates DelegationToken(DT, owner=A), then A loses lease (epoch -> 43) and another node B becomes owner. prefetch may still call into A using DT for in-flight warmups. If A serves stale KV entries then the runtime can surface wrong data to the caller.

lee: hmm — isn't DelegationToken supposed to be tied to an epoch in the token? we added token.epoch but we didn't wire validation everywhere.

maria: exactly. token currently contains {owner_id, token_id, created_at} but not epoch.

sam: options: add epoch to token and require owner validate token. or make delegation synchronous (block until handoff completes). both have tradeoffs.

nath: synchronous handoff kills latency for bursts. adding epoch to token seems lightweight but we need to decide failure semantics when epoch mismatch. do we retry? fallback to remote read?

lee: propose: token = {owner, epoch, ttl}; owner validates token. if epoch mismatch owner returns TOKEN_STALE. prefetch then either: 1) if local cached copy exists and is within consistency window, use local; 2) otherwise escalate to coordinator to re-resolve owner and retry.

aj: that implies two new response codes: TOKEN_STALE and TOKEN_INVALID. TOKEN_INVALID = token forged/unknown. TOKEN_STALE = owner changed epochs.

maria: agree but watch race: owner A could validate epoch and return OK, then immediately step down and evict the prefix before serving. we need to ensure read-after-validate still sees the same residency. meaning owner must perform validation+serve under a single lease-protected path.

sam: can we move validation into the lease check path so it's atomic? pseudo:
```
if (!lease.holds(request.prefix, token.epoch)) return TOKEN_STALE;
serve_value();
```
This forces owner to consult current lease index.

lee: that looks right. but cost: every delegated prefetch request pays a lease lookup and possibly a lock. performance hit but probably acceptable if token hits are rare compared to local warmups.

cache-bot: deploy-note — we already have a cheap lease-cache (best-effort) used by readers; would that suffice for the check?

maria: best-effort lease-cache can have staleness; we need a canonical authoritative check on the owner process. either call owner local lease store or a fast RPC to lease-manager.

nath: fallback behavior detail: when TOKEN_STALE, prefetch SHOULD re-resolve owner via resolver.getOwner(prefix) and then reissue a delegated request to new owner. If new owner denies (race), prefetch should fall back to conservative path: reject delegation and route request via sequencer (i.e., force a cache miss path).

aj: for metrics we should emit: delegation_attempts, token_stale_count, token_invalid_count, delegation_fallback_count. also latency buckets split by path (fast-validated, re-resolve, conservative).

sam: another angle — what if delegation tokens are short-lived (10s) and prefetches are low-latency so races are rare? ttl helps but doesn't remove the atomicity requirement.

lee: long term: consider a handoff protocol where ownership transfer carries a drain window: owner A remains authoritative for "reads of already-delegated tokens" until deadline X, then only after X will new owner B inspect. That gives strong safety but complicates lease handover and increases tail of two owners.

maria: I don't love forced drain windows — that extends disagreement window and affects capacity for hot prefixes. prefer token-epoch + atomic validate+serve + explicit re-resolve fallback.

nath: implementation checklist:
- extend DelegationToken with epoch and ttl
- owner validate path: atomic lease.check_and_serve(token.epoch)
- define RPC error codes TOKEN_STALE/TOKEN_INVALID
- prefetch: on TOKEN_STALE -> resolver.getOwner -> retry once -> fallback to sequencer path with metric tag
- add metrics & alerts for token_stale_rate > threshold

sam: testing: add unit tests for validate+serve atomicity, integrate chaos test where lease flips mid-delegation, ensure no stale reads observed.

lee: also add canary with opt-in flag (prefetch.delegation_epoch_check = true) so we can roll slowly.

maria: nice. I'll sketch a small RFC section and add the checklist + sample return codes. will anyone volunteer to own the prototype for the canary?

aj: I can take prototype. aim to have PR with token schema + basic validate path by end of next sprint.

maria: awesome. i'll add tests and the chaos scenario to the plan. thanks all. :thumbsup:
